description: We're STAMINA (Stellar Transmission and Monitoring via Illumination of Necessary Assets), working on the CLPS Lunar Mission Browser challenge. Looking for skills in: Python/API (NASA ephemeris data), Frontend/UI/visualization (Streamlit, Plotly, web/design), GitHub/version control, geospatial/planetary science, and presentation.
summary:
STAMINA is an interactive lunar exploration tool that helps users investigate where and when future missions could operate. It brings lunar maps, terrain data and Sun and Earth visibility into one interface, allowing users to select sites, explore mission timelines and compare conditions.

Using NASA lunar datasets and SPICE, STAMINA estimates how terrain affects visibility at a chosen location. Users can also explore south-polar temperature data and apply custom requirements.

By making complex scientific data easier to explore, STAMINA helps students, researchers and mission teams understand the trade-offs involved in selecting a lunar site.
details:
What it does

Choosing a lunar site involves more than finding a place to land. Sunlight affects available solar power, terrain can obstruct views, and visibility of Earth is relevant to direct communication. These conditions also change over time.

STAMINA brings these factors together in an interactive environment. Users can explore 2D maps and a 3D lunar globe, select existing sites or enter their own coordinates, and examine Sun and Earth visibility over a chosen mission period. Timelines show when each body is visible, while site comparisons and custom filters help users investigate different requirements.

How it works

The platform uses NASA’s Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) elevation data to represent lunar terrain and SPICE kernels to calculate Sun and Earth positions. For a selected site, the backend estimates the surrounding terrain horizon and compares it with the position of each body over time. The interface also provides lunar imagery and a Diviner temperature layer for the south-polar region.

Tools and creativity

We built STAMINA with React, TypeScript, Vite and CesiumJS for the interface, and Python, FastAPI, NumPy, Rasterio and SpiceyPy for data processing and analysis. Our approach combines scientific datasets with an accessible map, interactive filters and mission timelines, allowing users to explore trade-offs rather than relying on a single static map.

Impact and limitations

STAMINA is intended as an exploratory and educational tool that can support early discussions about lunar mission planning. Its results are estimates: visibility depends on the available terrain data and model resolution, and Earth visibility alone does not guarantee a communication link. Temperature coverage is currently focused on the south-polar region.
